💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack.
  • Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.
  • According to recent reports, however, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack. As a certified personal trainer and nutrition coach, I’d put a high-quality whey protein powder and one of the best creatines at the top.

Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.

According to recent reports, however, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps. The strongest pre-workouts stand out from the pack because they are formulated with research-backed doses of four key ingredients — caffeine (at least 200 milligrams), L-citrulline (at least 4,000 milligrams), beta-alanine (at least 3,200 milligrams), and betaine (at least 2,500 milligrams) — for physical and mental performance enhancement.

To save you the trouble of sipping on something that won’t give you an effective muscle pump, our team of expert product testers tried more than 80 pre-workouts and reported which supplements delivered the most focus, power, and tingles. Then, with some guidance from a few other experts, our squad of CPTs, CNCs, CrossFit enthusiasts, and dedicated weightlifters narrowed down the list to the eight strongest pre-workouts so you can select the perfect match for your goals and preferences.

It has been revealed that medical disclaimer: This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any latest supplement or exercise regimen.

Industry observers note that if your goal is to improve your athletic performance and power output in the gym, then we recommend Transparent Labs BULK BLACK. This supplement contains a potent combination of 4,000 milligrams of beta-alanine, 2,500 milligrams of betaine anhydrous, and 10 other active ingredients. Beta-alanine, a nonessential amino acid, may improve potential power output by reducing muscle fatigue, allowing you to push out a few more reps while you exercise. And studies show betaine anhydrous may improve muscular endurance. These ingredients work together to enhance your training, paving the way for strength gains over time.

Each serving of BULK BLACK also contains 350 milligrams of caffeine, which is close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Overall, the impressive formulation earns 4 out of 5 stars from our team, as we docked a point for the high caffeine content since it may be too intense for some people.

However, this high-stim pre-workout is certainly effective.

In a recent development, cory Kessler, C.P.T., C.F.N.C., has tried more than 25 pre-workouts. He tested the Blue Raspberry flavor of BULK BLACK before a cardio workout, noting that he felt more energized and focused throughout his workout. “I started sweating almost immediately, and within five to 10 minutes, I had a boost of energy, a massive pump, and felt like I could lift harder and stronger,” he says. Cory also experienced the tingling sensation common with high doses of beta-alanine.

Industry observers note that cory also enjoys using BULK BLACK before bodybuilding workouts since it contains 8,000 milligrams of citrulline malate. While more research is needed, some studies suggest citrulline malate may boost exercise and muscular performance.

Two other areas where BULK BLACK stands out: solubility and taste. Our team gave Transparent Labs perfect scores in both categories.

“BULK BLACK completely dissolved in my shaker bottle in only a few seconds with no clumps, grittiness, or residue,” Cory indicates.

Sources indicate that available in eight flavors ranging from Black Cherry to Watermelon Peach to Strawberry Mango, one of our other product testers chose the Blue Raspberry option, giving it 5 out of 5 stars for taste. However, there are some mixed reviews on Amazon about the taste, depending on which flavor you choose.

“It’s hard to describe the taste of Blue Raspberry, but that’s exactly what it tastes like. Not too sweet, which is a good thing,” he notes.

Related: Transparent Labs BCAA Glutamine Review.

Legion Pulse is our pick for the strongest natural pre-workout because it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors and contains six active ingredients that support enhanced energy.

As a CPT and CNC, I look for four main ingredients in a high-quality pre-workout supplement: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. Each plays a key role in enhancing athletic performance. Research reveals:.

Recent findings suggest that legion Pulse contains all four, including 350 milligrams of caffeine per serving, which is very close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Keep in mind that if you decide to try Pulse, it’s a good idea to monitor your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee or tea.

Industry observers note that “To get the most out of pre-workout supplements without stomach issues, start with a lower dose to see how your body reacts,” states Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD. “Choose supplements with fewer stimulants if caffeine bothers you, or go for stimulant-free options.”.

It has been revealed that luckily, if you’re fresh to pre-workout or are caffeine-sensitive, you can also choose the non-stim version of Pulse. So, even though we’d like to see creatine in the formulation, we still give this a strong score of 4 out of 5 stars, especially since there’s a caffeine-free version.

One of our product testers has tried five different brands of pre-workout and puts Pulse atop her list because of its effectiveness.

Sources indicate that “I’ve been using Pulse three times a week for six months, and it always makes me feel energized and focused,” our tester says. “My goal is to improve my personal records and lift harder, so Pulse is my go-to when I train.”.

She reports that it typically takes 15 minutes for this high-stim pre-workout to kick in, and while it does give her tingles, it’s not overwhelming. “I never feel a drop-off, but rather a slow energy release,” she states.

Pulse comes in 22 flavors, including Pink Lemonade, Cherry Limeade, and Strawberry Kiwi, so there’s something to satisfy everyone’s taste buds. That stated, one of our testers gave Pulse 4 out of 5 stars for taste, noting that while it tastes sweet, there’s a “weird aftertaste.”.

In a recent development, while the formulation and flavor options make this a top-rated pre-workout, Pulse is by no means a budget-friendly option. At around $45 for a 20-serving tub, it earns the lowest score of 1 out of 5 stars for price per serving.

While many strong pre-workouts cost around $2 per serving, Nutricost Pre-X is our pick for the strongest budget pre-workout because it costs less than half of that. At about $0.93 per serving, one tester called it “the best value on the market,” and I agree, giving this a perfect score of 5 out of 5 for price per serving.

According to recent reports, although some budget pre-workouts lack key ingredients, Pre-X contains the four main ones we like to see in a pre-workout: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. “The price is better than most other pre-workouts I’ve tried, especially for a supplement this good,” claims one tester.

In a recent development, each serving of Pre-X has 300 milligrams of caffeine and 4,000 milligrams of L-citrulline, so you should feel energized and get a good pump with this pre-workout. “I got a decent pump and had a calm focus without feeling overstimulated,” one tester indicates.

Some testers say Pre-X has a slightly lower dosage of beta-alanine than some other pre-workouts on our list, but others say they experienced noticeable tingles during their workout.

While testers did not experience any negative side effects when trying Pre-X, this pre-workout is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose. Some health experts have raised concerns about taking sucralose in high doses. As a CPT and someone who pays close attention to everything I put in my body, I tend to steer clear of artificial sweeteners. Because of this, we docked a point off the formulation score, giving Pre-X 4 out of 5 stars.

According to recent reports, nutricost Pre-X comes in five flavors, including Blue Raspberry, Peach Mango, and Watermelon. Collectively, our team gave this strong pre-workout 4.5 out of 5 stars for taste.

In a recent development, “This tastes great ice cold or at room temperature. I look forward to drinking it before my workouts,” notes one tester who tried Blue Raspberry.

Another tester who tried Peach Mango also gave Pre-X his stamp of approval.

“No artificial sweetener taste at all. It has a nice flavor that’s not overly sweet.”.

In a recent development, whether you like a strong pre-workout that’s sweet, sour, fruity, or tart, Jacked Factory NitroSurge has a fit for you. With 11 options, you can stick to your favorite or keep a few flavors in rotation to keep your taste buds on their proverbial toes. Between the deep lineup and satisfying flavors, NitroSurge earned a perfect score for taste.

One of our testers tried Strawberry Margarita, and let’s just say she was more than satisfied with her sipping experience.

“It’s wildly delicious. I’d drink this by the side of the pool over ice all day.”.

Another tester prefers Jacked Factory NitroSurge to some other strong pre-workouts he’s tried. “I did not like the Pink Lemonade flavor of Legion Pulse, but I would definitely use the Grape NitroSurge again,” he says.

In a recent development, as for its effectiveness? For one of our product testers, it took about 20 minutes to feel NitroSurge kick in. At that point, he felt like he could lift harder.

“I usually work out in the morning because I feel most rested then, but even after taking this in the afternoon, I felt ‘jacked up’ and ready to go,” he says, adding that he experienced tingles and a slight drop off, but neither was overwhelming.

Sources indicate that another tester who regularly takes strong pre-workouts doubled the dosage. He noted he got “a bit of a boost from it” but nothing like what you’ll get from other strong pre-workouts. Ultimately, this makes NitroSurge a solid choice for beginners, as you can see how you respond to a single serving before upping it to two scoops.

Sources indicate that besides the taste, I like that it’s budget-friendly while still including evidence-backed ingredients, like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, caffeine anhydrous, L-theanine, theobromine, and AstraGin. AstraGin, also found in Transparent Labs BULK BLACK, is a plant-based compound formulated to enhance nutrient absorption. While AstraGin is safe at 0.5 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, more research is needed on the potential performance-enhancing benefits.

It has been revealed that like some of the other pre-workouts on our list, NitroSurge is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about taking in high doses. Also, Jacked Factory supplements do not undergo third-party testing, which ensures products include the ingredients listed on the label and nothing else. This is especially important for athletes who undergo drug testing for banned substances. We only gave Nitrosurge 3 out of 5 stars in this category since it is made in a Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP)-certified and FDA-registered facility.

Industry observers note that for bodybuilders, a “pump” is a sign of a successful training session. Increased blood flow to the muscles makes them feel fuller and appear larger and more vascular during and after a workout. A pump also promotes muscle growth by delivering essential nutrients and oxygen to the muscles as blood flow increases. While you can achieve a pump through high-rep sets, drop sets, and supersets, high-stim pre-workouts like Gorilla Mode are specially designed to improve your pump.

Gorilla Mode contains several pump-enhancing ingredients in each scoop, including 5,000 milligrams of pure L-citrulline (more per scoop than any other pre-workout on our list) and 2,000 milligrams of Hydro Prime glycerol powder. L-citrulline works to widen blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the muscles. Glycerol powder is rapidly absorbed by the muscles and draws in water, which can cause muscle cell swelling.

In a recent development, if you’re caffeine-sensitive or budget-conscious, this intense pre-workout may not be the best for you. Although one serving only contains 200 milligrams of caffeine, you will need to take two servings to get research-backed doses of some key ingredients, including creatine monohydrate (only 2.5 gram per serving). At that point, you’d be at 400 milligrams of caffeine, which is the total amount the FDA claims is safe for adults to consume per day. For this reason, we docked a point off the formulation, giving Gorilla Mode 4 out of 5 stars in this category.

Don’t forget that this also impacts how much bang you get for your buck. A 40-serving tub costs $60, and you’ll end up going through it that much quicker if you take two scoops before your training sessions. That would bring the cost to $3 per serving. So, from a value standpoint, we can only give Gorilla Mode 2.5 out of 5 stars.

On the other hand, this pricey supplement earned a strong score of 4.5 out of 5 stars for its effectiveness. One of our testers uses strong pre-workouts several times a week and tried Gorilla Mode before an upper-body workout. “Not only did I have a good pump, I also felt more focused. I knocked out a few more reps than usual during my workout,” he says. “I like the Fruit Punch flavor, although it was sweeter than I thought it would be.”.

While our tester enjoyed Gorilla Mode’s taste, he indicates the powder was gritty and difficult to mix properly. This is likely due to the glycerol powder, which absorbs moisture, leading to clumping.

Recent findings suggest that if you like feeling skin tingles after taking your pre-workout, check out Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train. I love the prickly skin sensation because it lets me know my pre-workout is kicking in and it’s time to train. This temporary side effect, called paresthesia, is caused by beta-alanine, which works to increase muscular endurance.

Intensive Pre-Train has 3,500 milligrams of beta-alanine per serving, which is more per serving than almost all of the other pre-workouts on our list. “Beta-alanine is found in most pre-workout supplements, likely because it helps reduce fatigue and improve endurance in the short term,” indicates registered dietitian Alex Oskian. “This is because it reduces acidity in the body, which comes from lactic acid build-up.”.

According to recent reports, our product tester used Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train before a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) workout and felt the tingles within 15 minutes. “These were strong compared to some other pre-workouts I’ve tried,” he says. “I felt good tingles in my hands and face, which lasted for about an hour.”.

Recent findings suggest that earning a 5 out of 5 for effectiveness, Intense Pre-Train is also available in a caffeine-free version for those who don’t want stimulants in their pre-workout. The non-stim version comes in Green Apple, which our tester states tasted more like a greens powder than a sour apple.

“I’m rather caffeine-dependent, so I didn’t feel a burst of energy. I prefer caffeinated pre-workouts, but this is a great option for a late-night lifting session,” she says. Other testers who tried the Fruit Punch flavor say they enjoyed the tangy taste. To enhance the flavor, Crazy Nutrition is sweetened with the artificial sweetener sucralose. With some mixed reviews on the different flavors, we give this pre-workout a 3.5 out of 5 for taste.

Onnit Alpha Brain is designed to increase mental acuity and focus. Testers say that’s exactly how they felt after trying Onnit Alpha Brain, which is why it’s our pick for the strongest pre-workout for focus.“What makes this pre-workout stand out is the cognitive effects. I felt significantly more focused after taking Alpha Brain than any other pre-workout I’ve tried,” notes one of our testers.

Other testers agreed, saying Alpha Brain helped them feel present and ready to work out without being overstimulated, leading to an effectiveness score of 4 out of 5 stars.

Onnit Alpha Brain’s formula differs from most other strong pre-workout supplements on our list — it contains nootropics, substances that enhance learning and memory. One of the key ingredients, NooGandha, is an ashwagandha extract that can reduce stress and enhance well-being by reducing cortisol levels in the body.

Recent findings suggest that another key ingredient, AlphaSize, may promote the production of acetylcholine, a powerful neurotransmitter that enhances cognitive function. However, studies demonstrating the effect of alpha-GPC on cognitive performance used 200 to 400 milligram doses per day, and a serving of Onnit Alpha brain has 125 milligrams.

The other unique ingredient in Onnit Alpha Brain is Dynamine. It works similarly to caffeine, by blocking the body’s adenosine receptors that cause you to feel tired. However, this ingredient is banned in all sports supplements in Australia. While Dynamine is still allowed for sports competitions in the U.S., it is possible it will be banned in the future. Competitive athletes may want to steer clear of this product.

In a recent development, one of our testers states Alpha Brain is only middle-of-the-road compared to other strong pre-workouts when it comes to physical energy. “After taking other strong pre-workouts, I usually experience a boost in energy. After taking this pre-workout, the mental effects were much more noticeable than the physical ones,” she says. That may be in part because Alpha Brain lacks ingredients like betaine anhydrous, taurine, and creatine, which can support muscle growth and recovery.

According to recent reports, we give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars thanks to the inclusion of nootropics, which are quickly becoming more prevalent in the supplement market. But be aware that this probably isn’t your best bet for boosting your physical energy levels.

Recent findings suggest that long before the days of gummy and ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-workout options, the most popular choice was the original C4. The latest version, C4 Ultimate, is more concentrated than the classic formula, combining both exercise performance and cognitive-enhancing ingredients.

One of our testers tried C4 Ultimate before a 30-minute HIIT workout, reporting that the caffeine blend got her zoned in before her training.

“I felt great throughout the entire workout,” she reported, giving C4 Ultimate a perfect score for effectiveness.

This high-stim pre-workout is sweetened with sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about. While our tester doesn’t mind a very sweet pre-workout, the Icy Blue Razz flavor was a little too sugary for her liking. Mixing it in more water than recommended balances out the sweetness.

However, another tester was blown away by the Sour Batch Bros flavor, saying it tasted “just like Sour Patch Kids.” Taking both of their experiences into consideration, we’ll meet in the middle and give C4 Ultimate a 4 out of 5 for taste, especially since it comes in multiple flavors.

It has been revealed that another plus for this product: It contains creatine — a popular supplement among athletes and bodybuilders for its ability to boost strength, enhance recovery, and prevent injury. Because of its performance-enhancing capabilities, some people like to take creatine in addition to their pre-workout. If you want the best of both worlds, we recommend C4 Ultimate.

Sources indicate that keep in mind that one serving contains 1.5 grams of creatine per serving, which is less than the recommended value of 3 to 5 grams daily. If you want to get the most performance-enhancing benefits from creatine, you should invest in a standalone supplement to help support your fitness goals.One final note: If you compete in a sport that requires drug testing, C4 Ultimate may not be the best strong pre-workout for you because it’s made with Dynamine, which is presently banned for use in Australia.

In a recent development, our team of expert testers includes certified personal trainers, nutrition coaches, and CrossFit enthusiasts. As dedicated lifters and lovers of all things health and fitness, we’ve collectively tried more than 80 pre-workouts, giving us a broad perspective of what’s available on the market.

We tested each supplement before a workout, and in some cases, for several weeks or months, to evaluate its performance-enhancing benefits, taste, and whether the supplement had any negative side effects.

Using a 1-5 scoring system, we rated each pre-workout on a variety of factors, including:.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of the testing period, we compared feedback to whittle our list down to only the best of the best. We also received valuable input from nutrition experts on what makes a strong pre-workout.

A strong pre-workout contains a combination of performance-enhancing ingredients in research-backed dosages. “Usually, the strength of a pre-workout is based upon the amount of stimulants it contains. High doses of caffeine (300+ milligrams) are usually a quick identifier of the pre-workout’s strength,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian claims.

In a recent development, however, the potency of a pre-workout goes beyond the caffeine content. Other active ingredients like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, and betaine anhydrous can impact energy, focus muscular endurance, and power output.

“Stronger via the amount of caffeine isn’t always better. If the goal is a bigger pump in the gym, other ingredients like L-citrulline may be better,” claims Alex. “Another common ingredient that can help a pre-workout feel stronger is beta-alanine, which may cause a tingling or ‘pins and needles’ sensation on the skin.”.

Sources indicate that it’s also crucial to remember that “strong” is a subjective term. For example, I can handle a full scoop of RedCon1 Total War without a problem, but I have friends who get too many tingles from a single serving.

“Everyone’s body reacts differently to various compounds, so what works for one person might not be best for another,” indicates Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD.

A strong, well-dosed pre-workout supplement may help you train harder by boosting your energy, focus, and endurance during intense workouts.

“There are a few things that are really helpful when you are looking for a great gym session: energy to do the work, mental clarity to help focus on what you are doing (not just to work the muscle, but to prevent injury), and a great workout,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian states. “Using a pre-workout may just help you achieve all of these.”.

Let’s explore the potential benefits of taking a strong pre-workout before you start your training session.

Sources indicate that caffeine is one of the most popular stimulants used in pre-workout supplements to enhance energy levels and improve focus. Almost all of the pre-workouts on our list use caffeine and L-theanine. Studies have shown when paired with caffeine, L-theanine may improve cognitive performance.

It has been revealed that “Most pre-workouts contain the stimulant caffeine in higher dosages. L-theanine helps counteract the unwanted effects of caffeine supplementation: jittery feelings and a post-caffeine crash,” Alex states. “You might see less mental fatigue, improved reaction time, and fewer headaches while regularly supplementing with L-theanine.”.

Recent findings suggest that I like taking a pre-workout to improve my focus because it helps intensify my workout and keep me #lockedin. Several pre-workouts on our list contain Alpha-GPC and tyrosine to give you that zoned-in feeling. Research suggests Alpha-GPC may improve cognitive function, and tyrosine may increase dopamine levels and cognition. One study found L-tyrosine helped improve people’s memory while they worked on a demanding task.

Recent findings suggest that A pre-workout may help you squeeze out a few more reps as you work to build strength and muscle. Two ingredients commonly used in pre-workout, beta-alanine and betaine anhydrous, may help reduce fatigue and support muscular endurance.

“Research suggests betaine anhydrous can improve muscle strength and power via increased total work capacity and improved protein synthesis within the body. Simply put, you can do more work, which leads to increased strength and muscle growth,” states Alex.

Another common ingredient, taurine, may improve your performance and power.

Registered dietitian Alex Oskian claims not every pre-workout is created equal, so it’s important to pay attention to what’s on the label. “Supplements are not regulated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This means the supplement might not contain all the ingredients you’re looking for and may even contain unwanted ingredients,” she says. Alex recommends looking for supplements that undergo third-party testing.

If you choose a high-stim pre-workout, be mindful of your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee, tea, or soda so that you don’t go over the daily recommended value of 400 milligrams. This will help prevent potential negative side effects like jitters, anxiety, or trouble falling asleep.

“Consuming caffeine at the end of your day may cause sleep disturbances, which only hurts performance in the long run,” says Oskian.

In a recent development, no matter which pre-workout you choose, it’s vital to follow the recommended intake guidelines. Remember, pre-workouts should not be taken more than once per day.

“Pre-workout supplements are generally safe for healthy adults, but they can have some potential side effects,” notes Dr. Raj Dasgupta, MD, FACP, FCCP, FAASM. “It is notable to start with a low dose and talk to your doctor before taking them, especially if you have any underlying health conditions.”.

There are a number of important factors to consider when deciding which strong pre-workout is right for you, including:.

Many strong pre-workouts incorporate a variety of active ingredients. When choosing a pre-workout supplement, consider your goals. For example, a bodybuilder may prefer a pre-workout powder that’s highly caffeinated and contains ingredients such as L-citrulline, betaine anhydrous, and creatine to help improve performance. On the other hand, an endurance athlete may want a pre-workout that has less caffeine but includes beta-alanine, BCAAs, and mineral electrolytes.

According to recent reports, whenever possible, I choose supplements that are tested by a third party for purity and have transparent labeling. Athletes who undergo drug testing should look for certifications from Informed Choice and NSF, which ensure the product does not include any banned substances.

Although we test all of the products we recommend, it’s key to check out customer reviews, especially from people with similar fitness goals and preferences. They can provide valuable insights into the product’s overall effectiveness, potential side effects, and the most popular flavors.

According to recent reports, “Recommended brands and products are ones that are highly rated by people and contain ingredients that have been backed by scientific research,” states Dr. Raj Dasgupta.

Recent findings suggest that “Taste plays a big role in pre-workout selection. If you don’t like a particular flavor, then you likely won’t drink the pre-workout no matter its benefits,” Oskian says. It’s also notable to consider the use of artificial flavors, colors, and sweeteners.

The price of a pre-workout doesn’t necessarily reflect its effectiveness. Understanding the ingredients list and dosage levels is notable to ensure you’re paying for a high-quality supplement and not just expensive marketing.

There are a few potential red flags you want to avoid when picking out a pre-workout.

I like to avoid supplements made using proprietary blends. These blends are combinations of ingredients, but the individual doses are not fully disclosed. This lack of transparency makes it impossible to assess the effectiveness and safety of the supplement.

According to recent reports, many fitness enthusiasts and athletes prefer all-natural ingredients and products free from unnecessary fillers or additives. “If sugar alcohols and artificial sweeteners wreak havoc on your stomach, make sure those aren’t on the ingredient list,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian indicates.

Athletes who compete in sanctioned organizations should make sure the supplements they use are third-party tested and certified banned substance-free.

Recent findings suggest that if you have big fitness goals, choosing a strong pre-workout formulated with safe and effective doses of science-backed ingredients is worth it to deliver performance-enhancing effects. Keep in mind that even the strongest pre-workouts on the market won’t make you run faster, lift heavier, or exercise longer on their own. These supplements are designed to help you put in the work at the gym to make gains and enhance your performance over time.

Ultimately, though, a strong pre-workout is only part of the equation to becoming the strongest version of yourself. At the end of the day, you have to put in the work, follow a sound nutrition plan, and prioritize rest and recovery to crush your fat-burning and muscle-building goals.

Yes, technically, you can take a pre-workout made with 400 milligrams of caffeine. However, that is the maximum daily dose recommended by the FDA. This means if you’re using a high-stim pre-workout, you may want to avoid caffeine from other sources like coffee, tea, soda, or energy drinks. Since 400 milligrams is the maximum recommended daily dose, I do not advise using a pre-workout containing 600 milligrams of caffeine.

A pre-workout can directly and indirectly make you stronger. A well-dosed pre-workout may help you add a few pounds to your lifts or allow you to push out a few more reps during your workout. However, real strength gains will come from consistent training, proper nutrition, and recovery. If a pre-workout supplement helps you stay consistent in the gym, it may also help you gain strength and muscle mass.

Yes. Depending on your sensitivity to stimulants like caffeine, you may experience side effects, including jitters, anxiety, or difficulty falling asleep. If this is the case, use a half serving or a more moderately dosed pre-workout to assess your tolerance.

What’s the Minimum Amount of Core Work Runners Need Each Week?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A powerful stride depends on having a strong core.
  • It has been revealed that but between fitting in runs, setting aside time for recovery, fueling, and living life outside of running shoes, it’s hard to know if you’re dedicating enough time to strengthening this key muscle group.
  • We asked experts for that magic minimum number, so you can boost your performance without carving a ton of time out of your busy schedule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A powerful stride depends on having a strong core. It’s basically the glue that holds your running form together and will make every mile more efficient, helping you hit faster speeds.

It has been revealed that but between fitting in runs, setting aside time for recovery, fueling, and living life outside of running shoes, it’s hard to know if you’re dedicating enough time to strengthening this key muscle group. So when your calendar is already packed, what’s the minimum number of core workouts you need to do to reap the benefits?

We asked experts for that magic minimum number, so you can boost your performance without carving a ton of time out of your busy schedule.

Simply put, every runner should aim to get at least two 10- to 15-minute core sessions done per week, says Yusuf Jeffers, NYC-based strength and run coach, Hyrox race director, and Nike Well Collective trainer. This is an adequate number to support your running form, build more strength and power, and improve overall running efficiency.

Recent findings suggest that however, several factors can adjust this number, including your running goals and the season you’re in, claims Holly Dickinson, UESCA-certified run coach, NSCA-certified strength and conditioning coach, and owner of StrideHer run coaching. For example, if building strength is your offseason goal and you’re not running as much mileage as you would during race training, you might increase the minimum amount of core work you do to three or four sessions per week. During a racing season, though, you might stick to two sessions per week.

As for the exercises you need, you can skip moves like crunches, which can stress your back and neck muscles and isolate just a few ab muscles (namely, the rectus abdominis or those six-pack abs) and instead, go for moves like planks, bird dogs, Copenhagen side planks, and glute bridges. These moves help with spinal and pelvic stability and core muscular endurance, and mimic running form—plus, they work 360 degrees of your core.

Jeffers recommends spending at least 30 seconds on each move, completing your core work in a circuit-style fashion (which means completing each move back-to-back with minimal rest in between) and repeating the circuit for at least two sets.

If you strength train regularly, you probably don’t have to do any additional core workouts because many programs often require you to brace your midsection and keep your spine neutral in order to do the exercise properly, Jeffers adds, which is basically like built-in core work. Think of weighted back squats, deadlifts, and bench presses, for example. You need to engage your core to maintain a stable spine through all of these exercises.

Many people tend to think of the core as just ab muscles, but your core is literally everything that’s not your arms and legs, indicates Jeffers. That’s essentially everything from your abdominal muscles to your glutes, pelvic floor, and back. All of these muscles work together to keep you stable on your runs and prevent form breakdown.

Recent findings suggest that “The stronger your core is, the better the transfer of power as you’re running,” Jeffers explains. “That can keep your form better over time and also improve running economy.” For example, marathoners who tend to slouch or lean too far forward in the final miles of a marathon may lack the strength and resilience in their core to keep their posture upright, which can then make running feel more difficult and lead to a slowdown, he explains.

You should consciously focus on your posture and form during moves like planks and glute bridges, Jeffers says. He urges runners to avoid compensating with other parts of your body in order to hold a given movement. For example, if you’re arching your back or sagging your hips in a plank, or you’re feeling the burn in your lower back instead of your glutes when you’re doing a glute bridge, these are signs you need to brace your core more and focus on a straight spine.

According to recent reports, additionally, avoid using momentum or trying to go through an active exercise with speed. “The second you feel like you have to use momentum or use other body parts to either hold a movement or to do the movement, that’s your cue that you’re not holding onto the form,” Jeffers adds. In that case, slow down your movement and focus on form rather than trying to reach a certain rhythm or number of reps.

“The convenient thing about core work is that it’s often done without any equipment,” Jeffers says, making it easy to fit into your schedule.

It has been revealed that for example, you can turn to bodyweight core exercises as part of a run warmup. Or you can add core moves to a strength session, like performing Copenhagen side planks between heavy squat sets. You could also save dedicated core work for the end of a heavy lifting session or for after an interval workout.

The key to reaping the benefits of a twice-weekly basic core workout is actually doing it regularly.

Oftentimes, you might look for a quick fix to a strong core, Dickinson says, but keeping up with simple, frequent sessions is more effective long term. “Putting in the hard work is going to pay off, and it doesn't have to look extreme or crazy hard,” she says. “It’s about that slow, consistent work.”.

Experts agree that planks, glute bridges, and Copenhagen side planks are some of the best moves for runners. Incorporate these three moves into a quick routine two times a week to improve deep core strength and stabilization for faster, more efficient running.

According to recent reports, why it works: Planks train full‑body tension and teach your core to support the spine, just as you need on the run. By adding in variations like leg raises or shoulder taps, you can challenge your core strength even more and make planks extra functional, Dickinson told Runner’s World.

Why it works: Glute bridges allow for full hip extension, which leads to less strain on your back on the run and more glute activation, which can help improve—and add power to—your stride.

Industry observers note that why it works: This move works the obliques and hip adductors, or the muscles on the inside of the thighs that help draw the leg in toward the center of your body, allowing for better knee alignment on the run. Plus, they help with pelvic stabilization, which is crucial solid landings and forward propulsion.

Industry observers note that kristine Kearns, a writer and avid runner, joined Runner’s World and Bicycling in July 2024. She previously coached high school girls cross country and right now competes in seasonal races, with more than six years of distance training and an affinity for weightlifting. You can find her wearing purple, baking cupcakes, and visiting her local farmers market.

The Best Smith Machine for Your Home Gym in 2025

📅 04 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3192 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Breakingmuscle

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Other than the almighty treadmill, there may not be a piece of equipment more synonymous with commercial gyms than the Smith machine.
  • In a recent development, however, you don’t need a gym membership to enjoy its benefits.
  • It has been revealed that with options spanning from traditional Smith machines to all-in-one home gym solutions, you might feel a bit overwhelmed about which direction to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Other than the almighty treadmill, there may not be a piece of equipment more synonymous with commercial gyms than the Smith machine. Boasting tremendous versatility and functionality, this muscle-building tool is popular among lifters of all experience levels.

In a recent development, however, you don’t need a gym membership to enjoy its benefits. While it may have not been a home gym staple years ago, the Smith machine has become a must-have for many fitness enthusiasts. Offering added protection without a spotter for your bench presses, back squats, deadlifts, and other strength exercises, the Smith machine is a wise investment for those trying to build the ultimate garage gym.

It has been revealed that with options spanning from traditional Smith machines to all-in-one home gym solutions, you might feel a bit overwhelmed about which direction to go. Luckily for you, our team of expert product testers did all the due diligence necessary to separate the cream from the crop. From analyzing the build materials to testing the smoothness of the bar path to assessing the value, we took the time to dissect each element in order to narrow down our list to just five.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, we got some valuable insight from Mauro S. Maietta, district fitness and education manager for Crunch Fitness, on the benefits and what factors to consider when you’re shopping for a Smith machine.

This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any new supplement or exercise regimen.

Sources indicate that if you’re searching for a multifunctional Smith machine that’s compatible with a ton of attachments, the Force USA G15 is the machine that can truly do it all — albeit at an expensive price point of around $5,500. However, there’s a reason it earned 4.5 out of 5 stars for versatility from our top product tester: you can perform a wide variety of exercises by taking advantage of all of its functionality.

Recent findings suggest that tipping the scales at nearly 1,000 pounds, the G15 combines a functional trainer, half rack, and Smith machine into a single, sturdy unit. Measuring over 6 feet wide, over 4 feet deep, and about 7 feet tall, the G15 earns a 4-star footprint rating. While there are more compact options, it’s still a good option for folks with limited space, especially considering the versatility you get.

Offering dual 289-pound weight stacks that keep it well-anchored, the G15 also scores 4 out of 5 stars for durability and construction.

In a recent development, “This thing is like a tank,” our tester says. “Once it’s assembled, it’ll basically be stuck in place.”.

Unfortunately, our tester wasn’t as impressed with the cable pulley material. Asthey’re made from nylon instead of aluminum, they don’t move as smoothly and won’t be as durable as their metal counterparts.

Something that separates the G15 from many competitors is its ability to go from a 2:1 or 4:1 pulley ratio. This gives you the ability to make the weight feel like half or a quarter of the actual weight. While our tester would prefer a 1:1 ratio for more effective resistance, he notes the 2:1 or 4:1 ratios “will be adequate for most people working out from home.”.

The G15 comes with a lengthy list of attachments, including J-hooks, safety spotter arms, multi-grip dip handles, a multi-grip pull-up bar, band pegs, and a low row footplate. If you want to unlock even more training possibilities, the $700 G15 Upgrade Kit includes three additional strength training stations, three functional attachments, a TV mount, and four storage shelves.

Two knocks against this ultra-versatile machine: assembly and value.

Although some of the parts arrive pre-assembled, our assembly expert recommends budgeting “at least 20 man hours” to get the G15 fully put together. And if you want to leave it to the professionals, you’ll need to pay an additional $800.

At nearly $6,000 on its own, the G15 certainly isn’t made for budget-conscious shoppers. Our top product tester gave it 3.5 out of 5 stars for value, noting that Force USA could use better quality components, cables, and accessories, including one of the key parts of this premium-priced unit: the built-in barbell.“The knurling is super passive and not going to allow for an adequate grip for the user if you were to go heavy on any Smith machine movements,” he explains.

Want to crush a full-body workout with a single piece of equipment? The Titan Fitness Smith Machine can be the all-in-one solution that allows you to train your upper body, lower body, and core in a safe, effective manner.

In a recent development, is it as versatile as the G15? No. Is it far more affordable? Yes.

For less than a third of the price, you can still get an excellent workout experience from the $1,7000 Titan Smith Machine. One of our more seasoned product testers used it for a variety of strength training sessions, highlighting how impressed she was by the smooth glide of the barbell and the angled design. In addition, this Smith machine is counterbalanced so you don’t have to support the entire 45-pound barbell like you do on other machines. Beginners will appreciate this, as the bar only feels like 15 pounds.

Unfortunately, like Force USA, Titan left our team wanting more out of the knurling.

“It’s fine for a Smith machine, but it’s definitely not the most grippy bar,” our tester indicates.

On the other hand, this machine earns high marks for its ergonomics. Our tester rated it 4 out of 5 stars in this category. She found the single-axis, angled design helped improve her muscle activation during lower-body weight training exercises like Smith machine squats and lunges.

Most importantly, she felt completely secure using this Titan machine. Not only was there no wobbling or shaking, but the bar moved smoothly, leading her to give a 5-out-of-5 rating for stability.

“This is a super stable machine; there was no give to it even when we were using heavy weights,” our tester says. “This was ultra-smooth.” While Titan priced this machine fairly, we’d like to see a better warranty. A one-year policy falls well short of what we expect from most brands. Plus, if you want to return a piece of equipment, you must pay the return shipping costs and a 20% restocking fee. That results in a disappointing customer experience score of just 2 out of 5 stars.

Industry observers note that don’t want a standalone Smith machine? Bolt Fitness has a space-saving solution in the form of the Storm Series Stinger Smith Machine Attachment. Compatible with any 3” x 3” frame using 1” hardware, this universal attachment can seamlessly integrate with your existing squat or power rack, opening the door to even more training possibilities.

Sources indicate that we rate this Smith machine attachment a 4.5 out of 5 for versatility, as it offers 12 different positions totaling 60” of vertical adjustments. That means you can promptly go from a steep incline bench press to a Romanian deadlift, making your workouts more efficient, too. Plus, we also like that this attachment has a 43” built-in multi-grip pull-up bar, giving you the ability to develop your vertical pulling strength and endurance.

Bolt also earns solid marks for construction, earning 4 out of 5 stars in this key category. However, our chief product tester warns not to expect quite the same level of craftsmanship as some better-known brands.

“You won’t see the same quality welds or powder coats from Bolt as you will from Rogue or REP,” he notes.

It has been revealed that like several other nominees on this list, our tester was also disappointed with the Smith bar’s knurling. The passive knurl pattern won’t give you a particularly stable grip, especially when using heavier weights.

“You definitely won’t mistake this for an Olympic barbell,” our tester claims.

It has been revealed that as for the price? At around $1,100 this is on the expensive side for a Smith machine attachment. For example, the Bells of Steel Smith Machine Rack Attachment is much more affordable at $800. We rate it a 3 out of 5 for value, especially since you already need a rack to use it. Otherwise, expect to invest a significant chunk of change to get a fully functioning setup.

Recent findings suggest that just because you can’t afford to splurge on something like the G15 doesn’t mean you can’t find a Smith machine that fits within your budget. If you don’t have a ton of financial wiggle room, the RitFit Smith Machine is the most affordable option that earned our stamp of approval.

As our top product tester puts it, “If you’re looking for a Smith machine and you’re on an ultra-budget, this is it.”.

At about $500 on Amazon, this machine is less than a third of the price of the Titan Fitness Smith Machine and less than a tenth of the cost of the G15. Of course, it’s not the most durable option on the market, but it offers sufficient versatility at a very attractive price point to earn a near-perfect value rating of 4.5 out of 5 stars.

Dubbed the “sleeper pick” by our tester, he notes that “the low price covers so many sins.”.

Before we dive into some of RitFit’s shortcomings, let’s highlight some of the strengths of this machine. First, we rated it 4 out of 5 for versatility, as it offers built-in low row and lat pulldown capabilities using a plate-loaded cable pulley system that holds 165 pounds. The RitFit Smith Machine also comes with several attachments, including a pin-on landmine row and two multi-purpose pull-up handles.

Secondly, it has a compact design that makes it suitable for home gym setups with limited  space. It also weighs just 140 pounds, making it easier to move than other options on this list.

However, our tester had several callouts about the RitFit Smith Machine that deserve mentioning. With cheaper build materials and a lightweight design, it didn’t prove to be as stable as he would have liked, earning just 3.5 out of 5 stars for both construction and stability. Needless to say, this isn’t the best option if you want to lift heavy weights. Still, considering you could pay around the same price for a high-quality Olympic barbell, the RitFit Smith Machine is a solid option if you’re on a limited budget.

Imagine if you could turn your squat rack into a Smith machine in a matter of minutes. That dream can be a reality if you’re willing to invest around $700 on the VTS Lite Rack Attachment from Bulletproof Fitness, a lesser-known fitness equipment manufacturer that’s caught our attention.

While we haven’t gotten our hands on this attachment just yet, it’s hard not to get excited about the concept and execution by Bulletproof. The Versa Trolley System (VTS) Lite allows you to convert your squat rack into a Smith machine using your own barbell. The rollers are made from UHMW plastic, an ultra-durable material we’ve seen used on other racks. This attachment only weighs 15 pounds, making the VHS Lite a more user-friendly alternative than the full-sized VTS, which weighs in at 24 pounds. From a construction standpoint, we feel comfortable giving the VTS Lite 4 out of 5 stars.

In addition, we like that Bulletproof offers a wide range of options to accommodate different racks. You can choose between a 3” x 3” pair, a 2” x 3” pair, or a 2” x 2” pair. You also can choose different hook sizes based on the diameter of your barbell. This optionality, along with the added exercise variety you get from using the attachments, earns a 4.5 out of 5 for versatility.

Set to be released in May 2025, we’re excited to see this product in action. If you want a more streamlined solution than getting a standalone Smith machine, this is an attractive space- and money-saving solution. Based on the price and versatility, we give it a value rating of 4 out of 5 — though it could go higher once we get our hands on it.

Latest Update: He Ran 3,067 Miles Across America to Set a New Record, Averaging 73 Miles a Day

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Doing his best impersonation of the fictional movie protagonist who developed a passion for running, Balser, a 35-year-old red-bearded and straggly-haired ultrarunner from Indiana, spent the past six weeks spreading messages of love, joy, and kindness on an epic quest to run across the U.S.
  • Industry observers note that averaging about 73.6 miles per day, the Kokomo, Indiana, runner left San Francisco at 5 a.m.
  • His intent was to conclude his journey on the steps of Latest York City Hall, just as Pete Kostelnick did while setting his TransAmerica Run record of 42 days, 6 hours, and 30 minutes back in 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forrest Gump has nothing on Cameron Balser.

Doing his best impersonation of the fictional movie protagonist who developed a passion for running, Balser, a 35-year-old red-bearded and straggly-haired ultrarunner from Indiana, spent the past six weeks spreading messages of love, joy, and kindness on an epic quest to run across the U.S. in record time.

Industry observers note that averaging about 73.6 miles per day, the Kokomo, Indiana, runner left San Francisco at 5 a.m. PT on October 10 and ran across parts of 11 states before crossing the George Washington Bridge and entering New York City at 11:02 p.m. ET on Friday night. After running a few brisk miles through Manhattan, he eventually met up with his mom, stepdad, and two sisters and slowed to a walk on the final few blocks on the way to his finishing point.

His intent was to conclude his journey on the steps of Latest York City Hall, just as Pete Kostelnick did while setting his TransAmerica Run record of 42 days, 6 hours, and 30 minutes back in 2016.

Industry observers note that the only trouble was that when Balser arrived in Lower Manhattan with a gaggle of two dozen or so friends, family members, and random followers, they found all of the gates to City Hall Park closed and locked. So instead, he walked to a point adjacent to City Hall and, like Gump mythically did in Monument Valley, Utah, he just stopped.

Balser officially ended his relentless push across the country at 11:45 p.m., which means he covered the 3,067-mile journey in a record-breaking 41 days, 16 hours, and 45 minutes—roughly 13 hours and 45 minutes faster than Kostelnick.

“I know it was about the record, but mainly it was about us coming together and being together and loving one another,” Balser told the group around him after he finished. “We shared this experience, and I am so lucky and grateful to be able to do this, and I couldn’t have done it without so many people. I am grateful for this life and I’m going to keep living it like I do. So thank you so much, it means so much to me to have your support.”.

Shortly thereafter, his crew and family members celebrated with some late-night New York pizza and, after devouring a slice or two, Balser almost immediately crashed into a deep sleep.

“And we didn’t set an alarm for 5 a.m.,” crew chief Sam Yeary remarked.

Balser caught the running bug in high school and continued running competitively as a middle-distance runner for Vincennes University. He went through some hard times in his early 20s and dealt with depression that took him to a dark place that had him pondering suicide. But with support from friends, a job as wellness and housekeeping director at the YMCA of Grant County in Marion, Indiana, and an immersion into ultrarunning races from 50K to 100 miles, Balser got a new lease on life and has been spreading joy ever since.

Sources indicate that during parts of 2023 and 2024, Balser spent nearly 10 months running the entire perimeter of the U.S. self-supported, covering 11,170 miles at a much more forgiving pace of about 40 miles a day. He built a substantial social media following along the way, picked up a sponsorship from newly introduced footwear brand Mount to Coast, and started planning the TransAmerica run he says he'd been thinking about for seven or eight years.

Sources indicate that he planned to start in the spring, but his training suffered after he got sick, so he postponed it and began looking for a place to work and train. That’s when Yeary, a friend he met at a few Indiana ultrarunning races organized by Meshingomesia Track Club, offered Balser the opportunity to live, work, and train at his 60-acre family-run regenerative farm near Bloomington.

Industry observers note that training regularly with Yeary, Balser earned some money to help fund his journey, wrangled up a crew of friends and began making plans for October. He knew Kostelnick, a two-time Badwater 135 champion, had averaged more than 72 miles a day in 2016 to shatter the previous record Frank Giannino Jr. set in 1980. Balser decided to commit to running roughly 75 miles a day, which meant 15 to 16 hours on his feet with a rotating crew in a van meeting him about every four miles.

His route closely mirrored Kostelnick’s, taking him across parts of California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Upcoming Jersey, and New York. He passed over the Sierra Nevada range, across Nevada and Utah’s Uinta Basin, over the Continental Divide at Colorado’s Cameron Pass, and down the Poudre River Canyon, across the Great Plains and through Northern Appalachia, ultimately enduring more than 140,000 feet of elevation gain.

In a recent development, things didn’t go flawlessly the entire way. He had some stomach issues in late October and suffered from nasal irritation brought on by dry conditions. But for the most part, he was cruising along and following his catchphrase of “movin’ and groovin’” without any major setbacks.

Industry observers note that “It was probably one of the toughest challenges any of us have ever done. It was absolutely insane,” Yeary told Runner’s World early Saturday morning. “We set a substantial goal this summer when he worked on my farm. We got to think big and dream big. He’s had this on his mind for a long time, but the stars aligned this fall, and we put together a blueprint to make it happen.”.

Balser was ahead of Kostelnick’s record pace from the start as his progress was tracked on the Breaking 42 website and Instagram.

He was greeted by supporters at numerous points along the way and often joined by runners who ran alongside him for many miles. Yeary remarked Balser and the crew were thrilled, humbled, and grateful to have so many Americans cheering on a couple of Indiana boys.

It has been revealed that “Even as a crew, we were blown away by him performing at that level,” Yeary stated. “It was hard, but it was necessary for us to treat his consistency for 70-plus miles every day like it was something normal. But we had to in order to keep things going. 70 miles is no joke!”.

In a recent development, balser’s effort developed an inspirational following on his way across the country. Social media engagement spiked over the final days of his quest, and more than 420 people watched his final miles through Fresh York City via Instagram Live. Among those following along and offering support and congratulations on the live stream were U.S. Backyard Ultra champion Mark Dowdle and two-time Badwater Ultramarathon champion Lisa Smith-Batchen.

It has been revealed that “As an amateur recreational ultrarunner, I am so inspired,” stated Weston Traub, a San Francisco runner who was following along on Instagram as Balser finished. “Seeing him push the limits of endurance reminds me how strong the human spirit is. I have all of these long Strava routes mapped out in my phone that I’ll do ‘someday.’ Nothing crazy like running across the country. Seeing Cam get it done makes me think, ‘Do it now!’ Sometimes next year doesn’t happen, and life gets in the way.”.

Balser wore a YMCA of Grant County T-shirt while running through New Jersey and into New York City on Friday night. As part of his Breaking 42 campaign, Balser raised money through a website and plans to give 100 percent of donations directly to that YMCA branch.

Recent findings suggest that “I know people really focus on the record, and, you know, that's a beautiful thing to go out there and set something,” Balser noted. “But the main thing I wanted people to know is just that they're beautiful in the way they are. When we come together to do things, especially if it's something that speaks to our heart and what's possible with that, it's endless, you know?

Sources indicate that “Keep your heart open and find the right people when your head's down to pick you up. I'm truly grateful. I have put my body through more than I probably would want to ever do, but, I know the reach of that, that love. Every step I take, every breath I get to take, it reaches more people, and that's a beautiful thing. And I think it'll ripple through my life and other lives. This record will be broken, but the feeling will last forever.”.

Brian Metzler is a Boulder, Colorado, writer and editor whose work has appeared in Runner’s World, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, Outside, Trail Runner, The Chicago Tribune, and Red Bulletin. He’s a former walk-on college middle-distance runner who has transitioned to trail running and pack burro racing in Colorado.

In a recent development, the Companion Pass isn't a points redemption — it's a status benefit. That distinction is everything, and it's the insight that separates people who get this from people who miss it entirely.

It has been revealed that here's how it works: Southwest grants the Companion Pass when you earn 135,000 qualifying Rapid Rewards points in a single calendar year. Once you hit that threshold, you designate one person as your companion, and that person flies with you on every flight — paid or points — for the remainder of that calendar year plus the entire following calendar year.

In a recent development, the key word is "earn." Points transferred in from partners count. Credit card signup bonuses count. Shopping portal purchases count. Almost every way you accumulate points counts toward the 135,000 threshold — except points purchased directly from Southwest.

Sources indicate that the pricing inefficiency here is a calendar arbitrage opportunity. If you earn the Companion Pass on January 2nd, you get it for the rest of that year and all of the next year — nearly two full calendar years of 2-for-1 flights. If you earn it on November 15th, you get roughly 13 months. The strategy is to time your credit card signup bonuses to post in January, maximizing your benefit window.

Chase Ultimate Rewards → Southwest Rapid Rewards (1:1, Instant) Chase transfers to Southwest at a 1:1 ratio and the transfer is instant — points appear in your Rapid Rewards account within minutes. It has been revealed that marriott Bonvoy → Southwest Rapid Rewards (3:1, 1-5 days) Marriott transfers at a 3:1 ratio (3 Marriott points = 1 Southwest point), and transfers take 1-5 days. This is a less efficient path — use it only if you have a surplus of Marriott points and no better option.

The most reliable path to 135,000 points is stacking Southwest credit card signup bonuses. Southwest's consumer and business cards frequently offer bonuses of 50,000-75,000 points each. A couple who each opens one card, or one person who opens both a personal and business card, can often hit the threshold with signup bonuses alone — before spending a dollar on the portal.

Recent findings suggest that since Southwest charges no fuel surcharges on award flights and points never expire, there's no penalty for building this balance over several months. If you have any self-employment income — freelancing, a side hustle, a rental property — you likely qualify. This is often the fastest path to 135,000 points for a single applicant.

The Southwest Companion Pass was practically invented for the FI-minded family. If you have a consistent travel partner — a spouse, a partner, a parent you visit annually — and you fly domestically more than two or three times a year, this benefit will transform your travel budget.

In a recent development, minimum points to get started: You need to earn 135,000 qualifying Rapid Rewards points in a single calendar year. In practice, this means you either need access to Southwest credit card signup bonuses (which requires good to excellent credit, typically 700+) or a substantial existing balance of Chase Ultimate Rewards points to transfer at 1:1.

Industry observers note that how it fits the FI strategy: The Companion Pass is a force multiplier. Every dollar you would have spent on a second ticket stays in your investment accounts instead. Over a two-year Companion Pass window, a couple who takes six domestic trips per year could easily bank $2,000-$4,000 in travel savings — real money that compounds.

Who this is NOT for: Solo travelers get zero benefit from the Companion Pass. International travelers who primarily fly non-Southwest routes won't find much use here. And if you're averse to economy class or require a specific airline's premium cabin, this redemption isn't your path.

In a recent development, the Southwest Companion Pass earns a **moderate difficulty rating** — and that rating is almost entirely about the *earning*, not the booking. Once you have the Companion Pass, booking is literally the simplest award experience in travel rewards: search southwest.com, find your flight, click "Add Companion." There are no partner airlines to navigate, no availability calendars to decode, no call centers to endure. It's a 5/5 on ease of booking for a reason. The moderate rating comes from **three earning challenges**: **1. The credit requirement.** Southwest credit cards require good to excellent credit. If you're early in your credit-building journey, this strategy may need to wait 12-18 months while you strengthen your profile. **2. The timing discipline.** Earning the pass is straightforward, but earning it in January takes planning. You need to apply for cards 2-3 months in advance and coordinate signup bonus posting dates — something most people have never had to think about. **3. The 135,000-point threshold.** This is a real number. It requires intentional credit card strategy, not casual spending. For a single applicant without a business card, it may require supplementing with Chase transfers or portal activity. **How to overcome these challenges:** - Start planning in **October or November** for a January earn target - Check whether you qualify for a Southwest business card — it dramatically simplifies reaching the threshold - Use the Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal year-round to passively accumulate qualifying points If you've successfully applied for a travel rewards credit card before and you have a consistent travel partner, you can absolutely do this. The ChooseFI community has helped hundreds of families earn the Companion Pass — and not one of them regretted the effort.

According to recent reports, open a personal and/or business Southwest credit card so that signup bonuses of 50,000 to 75,000 points each will post to your Rapid Rewards account in January. Call to confirm when points will post after your first statement closes.

Once signup bonuses post, calculate your gap. Transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards at 1:1 (instant) to fill any shortfall. Use the Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal for additional earning on everyday purchases.

Sources indicate that set calendar reminders for Thanksgiving, Christmas, spring break, and summer travel. Southwest opens its booking window 330 days in advance. Book the morning the window opens to lock in Wanna Get Away fares at the lowest point costs.

Industry observers note that the Companion Pass is valid for the remainder of the calendar year in which you earn it plus the entire following calendar year. If you earn it on January 2nd, you get nearly 24 months of 2-for-1 flights. If you earn it in November, you get roughly 14 months. This is why timing your earning to January is the critical optimization.

Yes. Signup bonuses, spending on Southwest cards, points transferred from Chase Ultimate Rewards, and points earned through the Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal all count as qualifying points. The only points that do not count are those purchased directly from Southwest.

In a recent development, yes. The Companion Pass works on both cash-purchased flights and flights booked with Rapid Rewards points. Your companion pays only taxes — typically $5.60 each way for domestic flights — regardless of how you booked the ticket.

This sweet spot was last verified over 90 days ago. Award availability and pricing may have changed — verify current rates before booking.

Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Companion Pass is the single most powerful domestic travel rewards benefit available to FI-minded families and couples. At a cost of 135,000 qualifying points — achievable through credit card signup bonuses and Chase transfers — you unlock nearly two full years of 2-for-1 flights on every Southwest route with no blackout dates and no change fees. A family of four taking six domestic trips per year can realistically save $2,000 to $4,000 annually, money that goes straight back into your investment accounts. Time your earning to January, stack your signup bonuses, and designate your most frequent travel partner. This is the redemption that makes domestic travel a rounding error in your FI budget.

#91632. Breaking: The Arizona Experiment!

Breaking: The Arizona Experiment!

📅 02 Nov 2023 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1431 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The thing that drew me to early retirement is freedom, and that’s still the best part of it.
  • Back in 2005, the primary reason for this freedom-seeking was being able to devote my best hours to being a Dad – I had a feeling my career in tech would be too demanding to sustain once the full-time job of raising children kicked in.
  • Recent findings suggest that eighteen years later, wow has that guess ever turned out to be right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The thing that drew me to early retirement is freedom, and that’s still the best part of it.

Back in 2005, the primary reason for this freedom-seeking was being able to devote my best hours to being a Dad – I had a feeling my career in tech would be too demanding to sustain once the full-time job of raising children kicked in.

Recent findings suggest that eighteen years later, wow has that guess ever turned out to be right. Early retirement has proved to be the most amazing, worthwhile adventure and it’s still just getting started. It was an astonishing thirteen years ago that I wrote to you about Little MM starting kindergarten, and now he’s done with high school.

It has given me the space to enjoy so many new experiences, working hard and playing hard sometimes, but also slowing things way down when necessary, to deal with and grow through some real hardships.

But now, with that child-raising phase finally almost done, I’m cashing in a few of those Freedom Chips for a particularly major change: moving to a warm sunny place for the winter to try out a new life in the walkable, bikeable, car-free community you’ve probably heard me raving about in the past: Culdesac Tempe.

According to recent reports, so on the first of December I’ll be packing up the essential clothes, tools and gadgets, and throwing my very best mountain bike onto the Model Y to make the epic road trip across the mountains. Just in time to escape the incoming Colorado winter. And my son will be joining me for the trip!

Looking for updates? I have added a separate tracker page here.

According to recent reports, we’ve booked ourselves a spacious two bedroom apartment there, for four full months. Little MM will be roughly alternating his months between Arizona and Colorado so he can still have time with both parents, while I’ll be there the whole time.

Sources indicate that A significant part of the fun is that this will force me to invent a whole upcoming life for myself, away from the easy comforts of the big community and plentiful construction sites that keep me so busy here. It will be both a big change and a significant challenge, which is exactly what all of us need on a regular basis to keep life full of meaning and joy.

So What Are You Going to Do in Arizona?

In a recent development, the exact details are still in the works, and I’d love to hear your ideas and feedback (see the “get in touch” note below. But here’s what I’ve got so far:.

Is There a Bigger Picture To All This?

Okay, you’re onto me. If I’m going to go to the trouble of typing shit into the computer and sharing it with you, there’s usually a purpose behind it other than just journaling my own personal life, and this another one of those cases.

First of all, there are the first-layer selfish goals: I want to have the best winter ever, meet a bunch of smart latest people, and I also want Culdesac to be a huge success so they will build more neighborhoods like this around the country and set an example that permanently improves the way US cities build and expand themselves in the future.

But even if you don’t care about all that, I also want to use this as a little statement about trying deliberate life changes.

Industry observers note that by throwing myself into a fresh community which aligns so nicely with my own values, I hope to serve as a reminder that maybe you might want to try the same thing. Or just try anything new.

In a comfortable, prosperous country like ours, some of the built in tendencies of Human nature tend to work against us, saying,.

“Hey – I’ve noticed we have plenty of food and reasonable shelter and that’s good enough. So let’s just double down on the Netflix, comfort foods, and occasional luxury purchases and that will keep us safe.”.

Instead, I want you to set your life treadmill to just a bit of a steeper, healthier incline setting.

It has been revealed that that means questioning the status quo and doing your best to keep at least one little experiment on the go in the background. Maybe that means forcing yourself to move to a better place, or taking steps towards getting a fresh job that gives you a better work-life balance.

In a recent development, the biggest move I ever made was leaving family and friends and my old job behind to move to the US, alone, at age 24. Looking back, I’m shocked I had the courage (and the organizational skills) to pull that off back then. I’ve become older and a bit slower, and so comfortable that it’s hard to imagine doing something so bold now.

Sources indicate that but even today 24 years later, I thank my past self every single day for doing it. My present life is an incredibly different and better thing because of that past bit of courage.

In a recent development, the spirit of positive experimentation might also mean starting to challenge your body more regularly – giving it harder work and exposing it to a wider swath of temperatures and movements. Or joining new Meetup groups to expand your circle of friends and experiences.

According to recent reports, it doesn’t really matter exactly what you do, as long as you point your feet in what feels like a good direction and just start moving. Create some purposeful change, which will surely feel a bit difficult, simply because change is hard. And hard things are good.

Future Arizona Neighbors: I’ll see you in four weeks!

It has been revealed that further reading: I’ve been reading books, doing life experiments, and writing about the value of strategic hardship for a while now. But the latest is a book called Dopamine Nation by the talented psychiatrist/author named Dr. Anna Lembke.

Industry observers note that to summarize: your brain creates a baseline for happiness based on the HARDEST thing you do, and then compares everything else to that. So if you do hard things, life in general seems fantastic because of this perspective. If you eliminate all hardship, suddenly even the pleasures of life seem bland, and you live a spoiled and unmotivated life.

It has been revealed that interested in stopping by for your own Mini Culdesac Experiment? They have a few short-term rentals available at rather reasonable rates (less than nearby hotels) – check em out at book.culdesac.com.

What will you do with your car?

I’m bringing the car just as a convenient electric moving truck to carry two people and four months of living supplies. Once I get there, I’ll find a safe place to park it offsite and live the full car-free lifestyle of Culdesac, much like I do when I’m here at home. I typically only use cars to carry really heavy stuff or for trips to other cities and states, but it’s even easier to accomplish this in Tempe with its location right on the light rail and with their onsite bike, scooter and even car sharing lots.

It has been revealed that my place in Colorado is presently set up as a two bedroom house on the main floor, plus an apartment with a separate entrance on the walkout lower level. When I’m at home, I use the whole thing as one home – the apartment just makes a great place to host a fairly constant stream of visiting friends. But for the winter I’m hoping to rent out one of these spaces to a friend or trusted acquaintance who will take good care of everything, while I leave the other section free for the occasional visits I’ll be paying to this area over the winter. Aside from keeping an eye on the place, it will be a great way to practice the age-old Mustachian technique of making money while taking vacations!

What Happens at the End of March?

Sources indicate that as it stands, I have no intends beyond this point. I’ll head back to Colorado for my home base, but with this being a upcoming phase of life I’ll be layering on new adventures. Aside from the two mountain properties that I’ve been helping to build out, I may end up with an MMM Mountain Retreat of my own someday. Conclusion: ongoing thoughts on the Culdesac experiment are here: https://mrmoneymustache.com/culdesac/.
